name: Deathfix
label: Dischord
lede: Brendan Canty, Fugazi's drummer, picked up a guitar and a microphone, found his keyboard player in the back of Bob Mould's Cadillac, and made a D.C. record in love with 1972.

eras.title: In the back of Bob Mould's Cadillac
eras.text: Fugazi had been on indefinite hiatus since 2003, and Brendan Canty was scoring films and running the Burn to Shine series. A long tour in Bob Mould's band put him next to Rich Morel for months, and the two found they loved the same year in rock: 1972.

years.big: "It's like I can scratch this big rock, pop, overblown orchestration itch."
years.h: Bob Mould's touring band puts Canty and Rich Morel in one Cadillac
years.p: [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]] of [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] on what the new band lets him do. Morel, of [[Blowoff|cffa8bae-d631-4cda-a54b-5b8224ec3b1f]], is the other half: they bond over glam and prog and start writing in 2009.
years.xp:
Canty told The Quietus they really got to know each other "riding around in the back of a Cadillac touring with Bob Mould. It was not your typical Fugazi tour!"

Back in Washington, Morel came by Canty's warehouse, a big room set up to record because Canty does much of his soundtrack work live. "We would be jamming and throwing ideas at each other," Canty said, and they felt prolific almost at once.

The touchstones were Bowie, early King Crimson and T. Rex. "Buried deep in this band is a love of mathy prog," he said, "but we are actually trying to write songs."

years.cap: Deathfix at Union Transfer, Philadelphia, January 21, 2012
years.src: Dischord · We Love DC · Hometown Sounds
yt: Live at Comet Ping Pong, December 9, 2011
years.h: Mark Cisneros and Devin Ocampo turn a duo into a band
years.p: Two years in, [[Mark Cisneros|78448563-93ad-4d49-be7f-95bf5fe60021]] joins on bass and [[Devin Ocampo|10bc183b-b6a8-4769-9e7a-0637d0f8a7a8]], of [[Faraquet|e866e006-4c80-4753-b53f-1bc5d88ccddd]], on drums. That frees Canty to play guitar and sing.
years.xp:
Dischord dates the expansion to two years after the Mould tour. The full band is on film by December 9, 2011, at Comet Ping Pong in Washington.

Live, Canty told We Love DC, Deathfix is "a big loud thing," with improvisation in the way Fugazi did it.

eras.title: A debut from the warehouse
eras.text: Deathfix's self-titled debut came out on Dischord in February 2013 and sounded nothing like Fugazi. By fall the band had played Coachella, made a video for "Dali's House," and swapped Devin Ocampo for Jerry Busher.

years.p: Seven songs cut at Canty's warehouse studio in Washington, from "Better Than Bad" to "Transmission." Glam stomp, prog detours, Canty singing lead.
years.xp:
Morel's dance-music background, from Blowoff, his project with Mould, shows in the keyboards. Canty told The Quietus he was "taking my foot off the brake a little bit" after Fugazi.

The Quietus interview ran March 5, 2013, weeks after release. Asked about the old band, Canty said the perspective on Fugazi had changed 180 degrees: "We were always halfway up the hill."

yt: Live at Fun Fun Fun Fest, Austin, 2012
years.h: From Fun Fun Fun Fest in Austin to Coachella's Gobi stage
years.p: Deathfix plays Friday from 1:10 to 1:40 p.m., two months after the album. Dischord labelmates the Evens and the Make-Up play the next day.
years.xp:
Canty told We Love DC that Coachella's people saw the band at Fun Fun Fun Fest in Austin, which led to the invitation. He also pointed to the long history between Coachella's promoter Goldenvoice and Dischord: "Goldenvoice did all of our southern California stuff."

The plan for the set, he said: "You get together with some guys and you write some songs. You try to make the best record you can." Back home, the band played outside the 9:30 Club on May 19 for Sound Bites, a D.C. Central Kitchen benefit.

years.h: Hometown Sounds premieres the "Dali's House" video
years.p: Rich Morel's namecheck song gets a clip in early September, ten days before Deathfix opens for Pinback at the 9:30 Club.
years.xp:
Canty told The Quietus the band already had the music, "a shuffly dance track," when Morel turned up with an idea about wanting to be someone's house. Morel's line: "I wish I was James Murphy's house - because you can steal ideas and Daft Punk is always playing there."

Then, Canty said, "who can we namecheck to keep the ball in the air the whole time?" Hometown Sounds called it the song that stays with you most from the album.

years.cap: Deathfix at the Black Cat, Washington, March 17, 2013
years.h: Fugazi's extra percussionist takes over Deathfix's drums
years.p: Jerry Busher replaces Devin Ocampo in fall 2013. He played in [[French Toast|f9e0402f-c675-46d9-985f-07001bba6480]] and added extra drums and percussion to Fugazi, so Deathfix now has two alumni of the same band.

eras.title: Canty's next room
eras.text: Deathfix never announced a breakup, but it has released nothing since the debut. Canty's next Dischord band, The Messthetics, put him back behind the drums, next to Fugazi bassist Joe Lally.

years.p: Drummer Brendan Canty and bassist [[Joe Lally|62046ffd-7d76-476b-bee5-b281b7575c6c]] team with guitarist Anthony Pirog for a self-titled debut on Dischord in 2018.
